items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The change is one clear line, `self._fqdn = socket.getfqdn().encode('idna').decode('ascii')`. It matches the existing style, and the idiom is already used elsewhere in the codebase, so it needs no comment.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Fixed at the source in CachedDnsName.get_fqdn, which is the right layer. But it adds another inline copy of `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`, the same expression already in sanitize_address, validators and html, instead of one shared punycode() helper.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Nothing is wrapped in try/except, so an invalid hostname still raises instead of being silently hidden. The result is cached once and there are no magic constants. The reference solution behaves the same way.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: The domain is converted once in get_fqdn, so DNS_NAME is ASCII for every email.encoding. The agent checked that 'localhost', '127.0.0.1' and 'my_host.example.com' come back unchanged. No error is suppressed, and the hidden tests passed (F2P 1/1).
